value.name: receives discharge order
value.description: Asha receives the discharge order and confirms Bridgepoint has a bed available for her father.
evidence: the discharge order landed in Asha's inbox and Bridgepoint's intake coordinator confirmed the bed at four-forty-one

value.name: watches father prepared for transport
value.description: After nearly six hours at her father's bedside, Asha watches the orderly verify his wristband and sees her father drift toward her without fully recognizing her.
evidence: Asha had been at her father's bedside for almost six hours
She watched the transport orderly check the wristband against the paperwork, watched her father's eyes drift toward her without quite finding her

value.name: feels aftermath of crisis
value.description: Asha experiences the emptiness that follows once the immediate crisis has finally been resolved.
evidence: felt the particular emptiness that came after a thing was actually done

value.name: receives urgent work messages
value.description: During the drive back to Philadelphia, Asha's phone fills with ignored messages from her firm and opposing counsel.
evidence: somewhere around the Delaware bridge her phone began stacking up the messages she had been ignoring since Tuesday—three from her paralegal, one from the managing partner marked urgent, and a forwarded complaint from opposing counsel on the Hatcher matter with a timestamp from that morning

value.name: conceals absence from firm
value.description: Asha reflects that she told her firm she needed personal time but did not disclose that she had effectively disappeared from a custody mediation and allowed filings to go out without her review.
evidence: She had told her firm she needed personal time.

She had not told them she had effectively vanished from a contested custody mediation she was lead on, that filings had gone out under her name without her review, or that a junior associate had signed something Tuesday afternoon that Asha herself would never have signed.

value.name: faces looming hearing deadline
value.description: Asha notes that the Hatcher hearing is scheduled for Monday morning, raising the stakes of her work crisis.
evidence: The Hatcher hearing was Monday at nine.

value.name: returns home and reviews complaint
value.description: After arriving on her block at night, Asha sits in her parked car and reads the complaint twice before going inside.
evidence: By the time she pulled into her own block the streetlights were on, and she sat in the parked car reading the complaint twice through before she let herself go inside.

value.name: enters apartment with work in hand
value.description: Inside her home, Asha leaves her coat behind and brings her laptop to the dining table to continue dealing with work.
evidence: Inside, Asha left her coat on the kitchen chair and carried the laptop to the dining table
